MOLECULAR GENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Regional Genetics Service

PATIENT DETAILS
Name: [redacted name]
DOB: [redacted date]
Hospital Number: [redacted ID]
Specimen Type: Peripheral blood
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

REFERRAL REASON
Testing for known familial pathogenic mutation in COL4A5 gene. Family has previously identified pathogenic COL4A5 mutation (duplication of exons 10-24), identified in 2011. Patient referred for carrier status determination.

CLINICAL INFORMATION
Adult patient referred for carrier testing of familial COL4A5 mutation associated with Alport syndrome. Family history significant for pathogenic COL4A5 duplication (exons 10-24) segregating in the family.

METHODOLOGY
Multiplex Ligation-dependent Probe Amplification (MLPA) analysis was performed using MRC-Holland SALSA MLPA probemix kits:
- P191-B1 COL4A5 (exons 1-51)
- P192-B1 COL4A6 (exons 1-2)

Note: Probes for COL4A5 exons 8, 25, and 40 are not available in the current kit version.

Reference sequences:
- COL4A5: NM_000495.1
- COL4A6: NM_001847.2

DNA was extracted from peripheral blood using standard protocols. MLPA reactions were performed according to manufacturer's instructions. Fragment analysis was carried out on an ABI 3730xl genetic analyzer. Data analysis was performed using Coffalyser.Net software.

RESULTS
Targeted testing for the familial pathogenic COL4A5 mutation (duplication of exons 10-24) was performed.

COL4A5 MLPA analysis:
- Exons 10-24: Normal copy number detected (ratio 0.95-1.05)
- All other analyzed exons: Normal copy number
- Quality metrics: All control probes within acceptable range

COL4A6 MLPA analysis:
- Exons 1-2: Normal copy number detected

CONCLUSION
The familial pathogenic COL4A5 duplication (exons 10-24) was NOT detected in this individual.

SUMMARY AND INTERPRETATION
This individual is not a carrier of the familial pathogenic COL4A5 mutation (duplication of exons 10-24). This result indicates that the patient has not inherited the mutation that causes Alport syndrome in this family. The risk of passing this specific mutation to offspring is therefore negligible.

The absence of the familial mutation significantly reduces but does not completely eliminate the risk of Alport syndrome, as de novo mutations or mutations in other genes associated with the condition remain a theoretical possibility.

RECOMMENDATIONS
1. No specific follow-up for Alport syndrome is indicated based on these results
2. Genetic counseling is recommended to discuss the implications of this result
3. Carrier testing and prenatal diagnosis remain available to other at-risk family members
4. Family members who wish to pursue testing should be referred to clinical genetics services

LIMITATIONS
This analysis is specific for the detection of copy number changes in COL4A5 and COL4A6. Point mutations, small insertions/deletions, and deep intronic variants would not be detected by this method. Probes for exons 8, 25, and 40 of COL4A5 were not available; however, these exons are not involved in the familial mutation.

Reported by: [redacted name], Clinical Scientist
Authorized by: [redacted name], Consultant Clinical Geneticist
